source.title: Inside the Visual Mind: Neuroscience-Motivated Concept Circuits for Interpreting and Steering Vision Transformers
source.authors: Tang Li; Yanlin Chen; Mengmeng Ma; Xi Peng

record.tranche_reason: The paper qualifies the claim that SAE features are canonical units, stating that features may absorb or compose concepts and are not guaranteed to map one-to-one to human concepts.
record.gate_note: The paper benchmarks SAEs and their interpretation, but does not test toy-model superposition, neuron capacity allocation, or LLM feature geometry. Its steering results are not evidence that SAE features are complete or canonical units. The SAE benchmark's plotted geometry and monosemanticity metrics are not described in enough detail in the text to determine those properties.
record.test_reason: The paper uses SAEs on CLIP-ViT-B-32 as a tool and reports only its own toolbox's performance: concept coverage, interpretation accuracy, localization and WaterBirds steering. The SAE benchmark compares SAE variants, with no neuron baseline or test of superposition. The feature-absorption remark is an unquantified caveat in Limitations, not a result, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors present ViSAE as a data-centric toolbox (probing images, concept vocabulary, circuit tracing) for interpreting, auditing and steering ViTs. Its claimed gains are 20× coverage efficiency, +28.7% interpretation accuracy and +48.2% worst-group accuracy. In Limitations they caution that concept labels and circuits are approximations, not guaranteed one-to-one feature-concept mappings.
record.recipe_differences: The paper applies SAE training and interpretation to vision-transformer representations; it does not reproduce the original toy-model experiments or their method.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE benchmark metrics are swept over L0 sparsity and expansion factor; the authors select BatchTopK-SAE with expansion factor 8× and L0 sparsity 128 for subsequent experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 5 SAE architectures, expansion factors and L0 levels on CLIP-ViT-B-32, the paper reports monosemanticity (roughly 0.3–0.45 top-9 image similarity) and decoder orthogonality. There is no neuron baseline. The SAE features are used for steering, with WaterBirds worst-group accuracy +48.2% when background concepts are removed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features in vision transformers are usable for concept-level steering. This is method performance, not evidence about superposition.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The feature-absorption and composition limitation is not quantified. The paper says its empirical evaluation focuses primarily on CLIP-style ViTs and natural images.
record.rows_left_out: Steering accuracy, concept-coverage, interpretation-accuracy, and SAE benchmark results were not included because they do not directly measure whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units. The plotted monosemanticity and decoder-orthogonality results are not described with claim-relevant outcomes in the text.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity-dependent transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
No LLMs, and no comparison of neurons versus SAE features. The ViT SAE benchmark reports SAE-variant metrics only.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not measured. Absorption and composition are mentioned only as possible limitations.
No test of one-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T5 and V5 limits_scope label are unwarranted. The study is T4: it relies on SAEs decomposing superposed representations and evaluates only its own pipeline. Its Limitations caveat about absorption and composition is unquantified and generic.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions; superposition geometry and sparsity-dependent transitions.
Whether polysemantic neurons result from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Feature distribution or SAE recovery in LLMs.
The paper qualifies one-to-one feature-to-concept correspondence, but does not establish feature stability or completeness experimentally.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-B-32
rows.operation_detail: The authors describe limitations of SAE feature-to-concept interpretation.

conditions.value: SAE-based interpretation; empirical evaluation focuses primarily on CLIP-style ViTs and natural images

rows.measure: Whether SAE features map one-to-one to human concepts
rows.value: Features may absorb multiple correlated concepts or represent a high-level concept compositionally across features; labels and circuit edges are approximations, not guaranteed one-to-one mappings.
rows.note: This is the authors' stated qualification; the paper does not quantify how often absorption or composition occurs.
rows.check: This is not a result row. It is the authors' Limitations caveat that features 'may still exhibit feature absorption or feature composition', with no measurement, value or baseline. It cannot support a V5 verdict. It is also generic to SAE methods rather than tied to CLIP-ViT-B-32 as a subject.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SAE-based interpretation in the paper's vision-model setting
reader_labels.reason: The authors explicitly qualify one-to-one feature-to-concept correspondence and describe the resulting labels as approximations (r1).
